title: Circuit Lab: pulse-coil RLC ring frequency vs capacitance
description: A capacitor charged to 24 V is switched (at 50 ms) across the pulse-coil bench's winding — its catalog R and L, wired in the Circuit Lab and solved by the C++ MNA solver — and rings as a series RLC. Sweep the capacitor over a decade and read the ring's frequency from the coil current's peak spacing: f = ½π·√(1/LC − (R/2L)²), close to 1/(2π√(LC)) at this damping, so a log-log fit of f against C has exponent ≈ −½. The coil's armature feels the ring's ⟨i²⟩ through the bench port. The energy books are judged from 60 ms: in the first substeps after the switch closes almost no energy has moved, so their ratio there measures the restart step, not conservation. Needs sim_core.wasm (no TS mirror of the solver). Simulated, not metrology.

expect.label: energy books close once the ring is under way: residual under 1 %

summaryExpect.label: LC ring: log-log exponent of f vs C ≈ −½
the 0.47 mF ring (the fastest) is at ½π·√(1/LC − (R/2L)²) = 211.6 Hz (coil R 0.18 Ω + switch 1 mΩ, L 1.2 mH)
